# tempa

Rust CLI that keeps one context contract (AGENTS.md + `.tempa/` + `tempa.toml`) and generates the files Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor and GitHub Copilot read.

## Stack

- Rust edition 2024, MSRV 1.85 (CI image `rust:1.85-alpine`); local toolchain stable.
- Workspace: `crates/tempa-core` (library, all logic) and `crates/tempa-cli` (binary `tempa`, clap, thin).
- Git is called through the `git` CLI (`crates/tempa-core/src/gitx.rs`), not libgit2.

## Commands

- Test: `cargo test --workspace`
- Lint: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- Format: `cargo fmt --all` (check: `cargo fmt --check`)
- E2E: `cargo build --release -p tempa-cli && scripts/e2e.sh target/release/tempa`

## Conventions

- TDD: failing test first, then code. Regressions found in review go to `crates/tempa-core/tests/review_fixes.rs` or the module's test file.
- Logic in `tempa-core` is pure functions where possible; the CLI only parses arguments and prints.
- All text in the repo and for users (CLI messages, help, README, templates, docs) is English.
- Every finding is a `Finding { code, severity, path, message }`; codes are stable, e.g. `drift.modified`.
- Never overwrite a user's file without proof tempa wrote it (lock hash) or `--force`.
- A target format changes only together with `docs/target-matrix.md` and its official docs source.

## Off-limits

- `crates/tempa-core/tests/fixtures/` changes only when a test needs new data.
- Do not edit generated files (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.gemini/`, `.cursor/`, `.opencode/`, `.agents/`, `.github/agents/`, `.github/skills/`, `.github/mcp.json`, `opencode.json`, `.codex/`); change the source, then `tempa sync`.

### One context contract and one workflow for every coding agent **[Quick start ↓](#quick-start)**  ·  **[Install ↓](#install)**  ·  **[Agent support →](docs/target-matrix.md)**  ·  **[Releases →](https://github.com/anggaralabshq/tempa/releases)** [![CI](https://github.com/anggaralabshq/tempa/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?event=pull_request)](https://github.com/anggaralabshq/tempa/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/tempa-cli?label=crates.io)](https://crates.io/crates/tempa-cli) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/anggaralabshq/tempa?logo=github)](https://github.com/anggaralabshq/tempa/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20OR%20Apache--2.0-blue)](#license)
![tempa importing a Claude Code repo, reporting per-agent parity, and absorbing a direct edit back into the source](docs/demo/demo.gif) Teams rarely use a single coding agent. One engineer lives in Claude Code, another in Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor or GitHub Copilot, and each reads a different set of files. Project knowledge piles up in one agent's format (usually `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/`), and teammates on other agents work without it: they miss the conventions, run the wrong commands, and output quality depends on which agent wrote the code. tempa keeps the contract in one neutral place and makes every agent read it, then holds every change to the same workflow: - **One source.** `AGENTS.md`, `.tempa/` (commands, subagents, skills, MCP servers) and `tempa.toml`. tempa generates what each agent reads: `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `.gemini/`, `.opencode/`, `opencode.json`, `.cursor/`, `.codex/config.toml`, `.agents/skills/`. - **No drift.** A lock file records what tempa wrote. Direct edits to generated files are detected, and can be absorbed back into the source instead of being lost. - **One workflow.** Every change is a task with a plan, an optional decision record, a changes entry naming the agent and model used, and a pull request body with the same structure, whichever agent did the work. - **Gates before CI.** Git hooks sync and check locally; the same `tempa check` runs in CI when you add it. Supported agents: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, GitHub Copilot. What each one supports, and where tempa has to fall back, is in [docs/target-matrix.md](docs/target-matrix.md); `tempa doctor` reports it per repo. ## Quick start **1. Install** ```sh brew install anggaralabshq/tap/tempa # or cargo, or a binary: see Install below ``` **2. Adopt it in your repo** ```sh tempa import # dry run: shows what would be absorbed from CLAUDE.md, .claude/, .cursorrules, ... tempa import --yes # writes AGENTS.md, .tempa/, tempa.toml, hooks; syncs every agent ``` No agent files yet? Run `tempa init` instead (`tempa.toml`, `AGENTS.md`, `HARNESS.md`, `CHANGES.md`, git hooks). **3. See what every agent gets** ```sh tempa doctor # generated files, gaps, protected paths, hook status per agent ``` Each engineer runs `tempa init` once per clone to install the hooks (it never overwrites existing files). ## Install ```sh brew install anggaralabshq/tap/tempa # macOS, Linux cargo install tempa-cli --locked # any platform with Rust 1.85+ ``` Or download a binary for macOS, Linux or Windows from [Releases](https://github.com/anggaralabshq/tempa/releases). tempa needs git on PATH. From a clone: `cargo install --path crates/tempa-cli --locked`. ## Daily workflow ```sh tempa task new add-invoice # branch tempa/-add-invoice + plan file # fill in the plan, then a human approves it: tempa task approve tempa decide use-sqlite # optional decision record # ...work with any agent... tempa log --summary "Add invoice endpoint" --reason "Billing v2" \ --harness pass --agent "codex / gpt-5" tempa pr-body # paste into the pull request ``` ## Commands | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `tempa init` | Create missing contract files and git hooks. Refuses repos that already have agent context; use `import` there. | | `tempa import [--yes]` | Absorb existing agent files into the neutral source, keep other keys of shared configs, then sync. | | `tempa sync` | Generate every agent's files. Never overwrites a file tempa did not write or one edited directly. | | `tempa sync --check` | Report drift without writing (for CI). | | `tempa sync --fix` | Pre-commit hook: sync from staged sources, stage outputs and the lock, block on drift. | | `tempa sync --force` | Overwrite generated files on purpose. | | `tempa check [--contract-only] [--base ]` | Drift, contract documents, task rules, then the `[harness]` commands. | | `tempa doctor` | Per-agent parity: generated files, gaps, protected paths, legacy files, hook status. | | `tempa task new ` / `tempa task approve` | Start a task; mark its plan approved. | | `tempa decide ` | Create a decision record. | | `tempa log ...` | Append a changes entry for the current task. | | `tempa pr-body` | Print the pull request body for the current task. | | `tempa mcp` | Run the MCP server on stdio (agents start it from their MCP config). | Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` findings, `2` error. ## MCP tools `tempa sync` registers a `tempa` MCP server (`tempa mcp`, stdio) in every agent's MCP config, so each agent can read the contract and write workflow documents that are validated as they are written. Turn it off with `[mcp] serve = false` in `tempa.toml`. `tempa` must be on the `PATH` of the agent process. Upgrading a repo that already has its own `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `opencode.json` or `.codex/config.toml` (files tempa did not write): `tempa sync` reports them as `drift.foreign` and the pre-commit hook blocks until you run `tempa import --yes`, which moves their servers into `.tempa/mcp.toml` and keeps their other keys. | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `tempa_context` | AGENTS.md, commands, subagents, skills, rules (protected paths, harness, required headings) and the active plan. Agents that cannot load a command or subagent natively read it here. | | `tempa_status` | Current task, plan state, changes entries, drift (JSON). | | `tempa_plan` | Fill sections of the current plan. Unknown headings are rejected; approval stays with a person. | | `tempa_decide` | Create a decision record; every required heading must be filled. | | `tempa_log_change` | Append a changes entry (same rules as `tempa log`). | | `tempa_check` | Run `tempa check` (drift, contract, task rules); `harness: true` also runs the `[harness]` commands. Findings as JSON. | | `tempa_pr_body` | Pull request body for the current task. | ## Rules worth knowing - Edit the source, not generated files. If you did edit a generated file, `tempa import --yes` absorbs it; `tempa sync --force` discards it. - The pre-commit hook only syncs from staged sources, so a commit never contains generated output for work you have not staged. - Plans are approved by a person (`tempa task approve`), never by an agent. - Configure the gates in `tempa.toml`: `[harness]` commands (format, lint, test), protected paths, required decisions, maximum diff size. Generated files and dependency lockfiles (`Cargo.lock`, `bun.lock`, `package-lock.json`, ...) do not count toward the diff size. ## CI Optional, and can come later. Local hooks can be skipped with `--no-verify`, so a CI step closes that gap. [`docs/tempa-devops.md`](crates/tempa-core/src/templates/devops.md) (written into your repo by `tempa init`) has ready-made Bitbucket Pipelines and GitHub Actions steps. Build the image with `docker build -t tempa:0.1.0 .`. ## Why tempa Your team's agent setup, reviewed like code. - **Edit anywhere, lose nothing.** A direct edit to a generated file is detected, and `tempa import --yes` moves it back into the source instead of overwriting it. - **Honest about gaps.** `tempa doctor` shows, per agent, what it gets and what it cannot load natively, with the official docs behind every format in [docs/target-matrix.md](docs/target-matrix.md). - **Gaps still reach the agent.** Commands or subagents an agent cannot load natively are served by the `tempa` MCP server (`tempa_context`). - **Enforced in CI.** `tempa check` gates the contract itself: required headings, protected paths, harness commands, diff size, decision records for dependency changes. - **One workflow, any agent.** An optional task flow (plan, decision, changes entry, pull request body) that looks the same whichever agent did the work. ## Development ```sh cargo test --workspace cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings cargo fmt --check cargo build --release -p tempa-cli && scripts/e2e.sh target/release/tempa ``` This repo uses tempa on itself; see `AGENTS.md` and `HARNESS.md`. An experimental desktop app lives on the frozen [`desktop-app`](https://github.com/anggaralabshq/tempa/tree/desktop-app) branch; the CLI is the product. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License Licensed under either of [Apache License, Version 2.0](LICENSE-APACHE) or [MIT license](LICENSE-MIT) at your option. Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution you submit for inclusion in tempa, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, is dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

# Contributing

Thanks for helping. tempa is developed with tempa, so a change follows the same workflow it enforces.

## Setup

- Rust 1.85+ and git.
- `cargo install --path crates/tempa-cli --locked`, then `tempa init` once per clone to install the hooks.

## A change

1. Open an issue first for anything bigger than a bug fix, so we agree on the direction.
2. `tempa task new <slug>`, fill in the plan (`docs/plans/<id>.md`) and approve it with `tempa task approve`.
3. Write a failing test first, then the code. See `AGENTS.md` for conventions and `HARNESS.md` for the definition of done.
4. Changing a generated format for an agent? Update `docs/target-matrix.md` and link the agent's official docs.
5. `tempa log ...`, commit (the pre-commit hook syncs generated files), push (the pre-push hook runs `tempa check`).
6. Open the pull request with `tempa pr-body` as its description. Keep it under 800 changed lines; split larger work.

## License

By contributing you agree that your contribution is dual licensed under MIT OR Apache-2.0, as described in the README.

# Harness

## Definition of done

- `tempa check` passes: contract documents, task rules, and every harness command in `tempa.toml`.
- A new test for every new behavior or fixed bug, shown to fail before the fix.
- `scripts/e2e.sh` passes for changes that touch a CLI flow.
- A `CHANGES.md` entry written with `tempa log`, naming the agent and model.

## Gates

- Pre-commit: `tempa sync --fix` (sync from staged sources, block on drift).
- Pre-push: `tempa check` (contract + harness: format, lint, test).
- Task pull requests target the milestone branch and are gated by the hooks above.
- CI runs once per milestone, on the pull request into `main`: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs format, lint and tests on Linux, macOS and Windows, and the end-to-end script on Linux and macOS. Contract and task gates stay local, per task pull request.

# Security

Please report vulnerabilities privately through [GitHub security advisories](https://github.com/anggaralabshq/tempa/security/advisories/new), not in a public issue.

Include the tempa version, your platform, and steps to reproduce. You can expect a first answer within a week. Fixes go into the next release; only the latest release is supported.

tempa writes files inside your repository and registers an MCP server (`tempa mcp`) that agents start locally. Issues in either area, such as writing outside the repository, overwriting a user's file without `--force`, or an MCP tool acting outside the contract, are in scope.

# Releasing tempa

A release is a version tag. `.github/workflows/release.yml` does the rest.

## One-time setup

1. **crates.io**: create an API token (scope `publish-new`, then `publish-update`) and save it as the repo secret `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`. Without it the crates.io job skips.
2. **Homebrew**: create a fine-grained personal access token with *Contents: read and write* on `anggaralabshq/homebrew-tap` only, and save it as the repo secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`. Without it the Homebrew job skips.
3. The tap and this repo must be public before `brew install` works for anyone else: the formula downloads the release archives anonymously.

## Each release

1. Set `version` in the workspace `Cargo.toml` (both crates inherit it) and in `crates/tempa-cli/Cargo.toml`'s `tempa-core` dependency.
2. Run the checks in `HARNESS.md`; merge to `main`.
3. Tag and push: `git tag v1.2.3 && git push origin v1.2.3`. The workflow stops before publishing anything if the tag does not match the version (`scripts/check-version.sh`).
4. The workflow builds `tempa-v1.2.3-<target>` archives (macOS arm64/x86_64, Linux arm64/x86_64 musl, Windows x86_64) with `.sha256` files, attaches them to the GitHub Release, publishes `tempa-core` then `tempa-cli` to crates.io, and writes `Formula/tempa.rb` in the tap (`scripts/homebrew-formula.sh`).
5. Check: `brew install anggaralabshq/tap/tempa && tempa --version`.

crates.io never takes a version twice: if publishing fails after `tempa-core` went up, bump the patch version and tag again.

# Agent target matrix (verified 2026-11-06)

Used by `tempa sync` (`crates/tempa-core/src/targets.rs`). Update this file and the code together when an agent's docs change.

| Source | Claude Code | Codex | Gemini CLI | OpenCode | Cursor | GitHub Copilot |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| context | `CLAUDE.md` = header + `@AGENTS.md` | native `AGENTS.md` | `.gemini/settings.json` → `context.fileName = ["AGENTS.md"]` | native `AGENTS.md` | native `AGENTS.md` (root and subfolders) | native `AGENTS.md` (CLI, cloud agent, code review, VS Code); no `copilot-instructions.md`, so it is not loaded twice |
| commands | `.claude/commands/<rel>` (md + frontmatter, `$ARGUMENTS`) | **gap**: custom prompts are deprecated and user-level only (`~/.codex/prompts`) | `.gemini/commands/<rel>.toml` (`description`, `prompt`, `{{args}}`; subfolder → `:`) | `.opencode/commands/<rel>` (md + `description`, `$ARGUMENTS`) | `.cursor/commands/<rel>` (md without frontmatter); *not confirmed by docs, see notes* | `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (`name`, `description`, `disable-model-invocation: true`; `$ARGUMENTS` → the text after the command); prompt files are not loaded by the Copilot harness or CLI |
| agents | `.claude/agents/<rel>` | `.codex/agents/<stem>.toml` (`name`, `description`, `developer_instructions` = body) | `.gemini/agents/<rel>` (frontmatter `name`, `description`) | `.opencode/agents/<rel>` (frontmatter `description`, `mode: subagent`) | `.cursor/agents/<rel>` (frontmatter `name`, `description`); not written when Claude is enabled, because Cursor also reads `.claude/agents/` (it reads `.codex/agents/` only as markdown, while Codex's files there are TOML) | `.github/agents/<stem>.agent.md` (`name`, `description`) |
| skills | `.claude/skills/<name>/` | `.agents/skills/<name>/` | `.agents/skills/<name>/` (official alias `.gemini/skills`) | `.agents/skills/<name>/` | `.agents/skills/<name>/` | `.agents/skills/<name>/` |
| mcp | `.mcp.json` `mcpServers` | `.codex/config.toml` `[mcp_servers.<name>]` (`command`, `args`, `env` / `url`; trusted projects only) | `.gemini/settings.json` `mcpServers` | `opencode.json` `mcp` (`type: "local"`, `command: [..]`, `environment` / `type: "remote"`, `url`) | `.cursor/mcp.json` `mcpServers`, `${VAR}` → `${env:VAR}` | `.github/mcp.json` `mcpServers` (`type: "local"`/`"http"`, `tools: ["*"]`, `${VAR}` as is); the cloud agent is configured only in the repo UI, so it is not covered |
| settings-deny | `.claude/settings.json` `permissions.deny` `Edit(/<path>)` | **gap**: permissions (beta) apply only to sandboxed commands | **gap**: workspace `.gemini/policies` are ignored | `opencode.json` `permission.edit` `{"*": <user default>, "<glob>": "deny"}` (root-relative globs not confirmed by docs) | `.cursor/cli.json` `permissions.deny` `Write(<glob>)`; Cursor CLI only, the IDE still relies on CI | **gap**: no repo-level deny (managed settings only) |

## Notes

- `.agents/skills/` is read by Codex, Gemini, OpenCode and Cursor, so it is written once. OpenCode and Cursor also read `.claude/skills/`, so the same skill is visible from two places with identical content. Accepted: `tempa sync` keeps them identical.
- Claude: `Edit(...)` covers every file-writing tool (Write, MultiEdit). `/path` in project settings is relative to the project root, matching the root-relative `protected_paths` globs used in CI.
- Gemini CLI: for free-tier and Google One users, Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI on 2026-06-18. This target still applies to paid and enterprise Gemini CLI users.
- Cursor commands: the commands docs page points to Skills, and Cursor offers a command → skill migration (`disable-model-invocation: true`). `.cursor/commands/` stays for now; move to skills when Cursor stops reading it.
- MCP env and headers: the source uses Claude's `${VAR}` syntax. OpenCode → `{env:VAR}`. Codex passes `env` and `http_headers` through: `KEY = "${KEY}"` → `env_vars = ["KEY"]`, header `"${VAR}"` → `env_http_headers`, `Authorization: "Bearer ${VAR}"` → `bearer_token_env_var`; any other form (e.g. `DB = "${DB_URL}"`, a rename) is reported as an `mcp` gap. Gemini: `${VAR}` passes through (docs support `$VAR` and `${VAR}`). Cursor: `${VAR}` is rewritten to `${env:VAR}` in every server string (command, args, env, url, headers), except Cursor's own `${workspaceFolder}`, `${workspaceFolderBasename}`, `${userHome}`, `${pathSeparator}` and `${/}`; `tempa import` turns `${env:VAR}` back into `${VAR}`. Copilot: `tempa import` absorbs servers from `.github/mcp.json`; a `tools` list other than `["*"]` is reported as a gap.
- Cursor reads `AGENTS.md` itself (official docs), so `.cursor/rules/tempa.mdc` is no longer generated; `tempa sync` deletes an old copy unless it was edited by hand (per the lock).
- `tempa` server: `tempa sync` adds `tempa` (`command = "tempa"`, `args = ["mcp"]`) to all six MCP configs above at render time, unless `[mcp] serve = false` or `.tempa/mcp.toml` already has a server named `tempa`. It is not written to `.tempa/mcp.toml`, and `tempa import` does not absorb it. Claude: `.claude/settings.json` gets `enabledMcpjsonServers: ["tempa"]` so the project server needs no manual approval. Codex loads `.codex/config.toml` only in trusted projects. Commands and subagents an agent does not support (gaps in `tempa doctor`) are available through `tempa_context`.
- Copilot: VS Code (since 1.144) uses the same Copilot harness as the CLI, so the targets follow the CLI/harness format, not `.vscode/mcp.json` and `.prompt.md` (the legacy Local harness). Copilot CLI also reads `.claude/skills/` and `.mcp.json`; with Claude enabled, the same skills and servers are visible from two places with identical content. Visual Studio, JetBrains and Xcode chat read only `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, so they get no context; `tempa doctor` still reports that file as legacy, to be moved into AGENTS.md.

# Tempa: CI setup (one time)

Local git hooks already run `tempa sync --fix` (pre-commit) and `tempa check` (pre-push). Hooks can be skipped with `--no-verify`, so enforce the contract in CI once you are ready.

## 1. CI step

The step only checks drift and the contract documents. It needs no secrets and runs no tests; keep lint/test in your existing steps. It needs the full git history (`tempa check` diffs against the base branch).

Bitbucket Pipelines:

```yaml
pipelines:
  pull-requests:
    '**':
      - step:
          name: tempa contract
          image: <registry>/tempa:0.1.0
          clone:
            depth: full
          script:
            - tempa check --contract-only
```

GitHub Actions:

```yaml
on: pull_request
jobs:
  tempa:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container: <registry>/tempa:0.1.0
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
      - run: tempa check --contract-only --base "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"
```

Set `<registry>` once the image hosting is decided. The image version must match `tempa_version` in `tempa.toml`.

## 2. Merge rules

- Require the tempa step to pass (Bitbucket: Minimum successful builds 1; GitHub: required status check).
- Require at least one approval.
- Bitbucket Premium: tick "Prevent a merge with unresolved merge checks".

## 3. Don't

- Don't accept a build status reported from a developer machine in place of this step.

## Context

The M2 review found two gaps that need tempa-core API: the desktop app (no console on Windows) flashed a console window for every git call, and the Absorb dialog could not list the targets an import overwrites.

## Options

1. Add `tempa_core::command(program)` (Command with CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows) and use it in gitx; add `ImportReport.absorbed`. 2. Duplicate the flag logic in the app and re-derive absorbed targets from drift there: two copies of the rules, against the spec (app and CLI share tempa-core).

## Decision

Option 1. The CLI behaves the same: its git calls capture output, so a missing console changes nothing for it.

## Consequences

Two small additions to the public API of tempa-core. Every new subprocess in core or app should use `command`.

## Agent + model

claude-code / claude-opus-5-5

## Context

The desktop app (app/) was frozen when tempa refocused on contract sync. Kept in main it adds 7.7k lines, Bun and Tauri to the pre-push harness, and a Windows-only CI job, and confuses readers of a CLI repo.

## Options

1. Keep app/ in main, frozen. 2. Move it to a branch and make main CLI-only. 3. Delete it.

## Decision

Option 2. Branch desktop-app holds the app as of m4. main drops app/, its harness commands and app-windows.yml; ci.yml tests the CLI on Linux, macOS and Windows for pull requests into main. The removal exceeds max_diff_lines and is pushed past the pre-push gate once, because it only deletes code that is archived on the branch.

## Consequences

Pre-push needs only Rust. The app can return from its branch later. The README points at the branch.

## Agent + model

claude-code / claude-opus-5-5

## Context

tempa shipped with Indonesian contract vocabulary (Tujuan, Ringkasan, ...). The CLI is going public and every other user-facing text is English.

## Options

1. Keep Indonesian defaults. 2. Switch to English and break existing repos. 3. Switch to English with legacy Indonesian aliases accepted everywhere a name is matched.

## Decision

Option 3. Defaults, templates, CHANGES fields and pr-body sections are English; contract::same_name accepts the Indonesian predecessor of each English name.

## Consequences

Existing repos pass without migration. New plans and decision records use English headings. The alias table is fixed; a repo with custom headings matches them exactly as before.

## Agent + model

claude-code / claude-opus-5-5

## Context

Agents other than Claude Code cannot load tempa's commands, subagents or deny rules natively, and each agent writes plans and changes entries its own way. M3-lite needs a way for every agent to read the contract and write workflow documents that are validated as they are written, without the M2 desktop host.

## Options

1. A stdio MCP server inside the tempa binary, hand-rolled on serde_json (already a dependency).
2. The same server on an MCP SDK crate (rmcp): more protocol coverage, but a new dependency tree and an async runtime.
3. No server: keep only generated files plus `tempa check` in hooks.

## Decision

Option 1. `tempa mcp` speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 with the tools subset of MCP; `tempa sync` injects it into every agent's MCP config at render time (`[mcp] serve`, default true), never into `.tempa/mcp.toml`. Public surface added: the `tempa mcp` command, the `[mcp]` table, the seven `tempa_*` tools and `drift.foreign`. serde_json is added as a dev-dependency of tempa-cli for the stdio test only.

## Consequences

No new runtime dependency and one binary to ship. tempa owns protocol conformance: only tools are implemented, and newer MCP features (resources, progress, cancellation) need code here. Long harness runs are opt-in on `tempa_check` because clients time out tool calls. Repos with hand-made MCP config files must run `tempa import --yes` once on upgrade (`drift.foreign`).

## Agent + model

claude-code / claude-opus-5-5

## Context

tempa is getting ready for a public release. The owner chose a dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 license and publishing on crates.io. The crate name tempa is already taken there (an unrelated animation-time crate).

## Options

1. Publish as tempa-cli (binary tempa) plus tempa-core. 2. Pick a new product name. 3. Skip crates.io (GitHub Releases, Homebrew, cargo install --git only).

## Decision

Option 1 (owner). tempa-core gets a version on its path dependency so both crates publish; keywords, categories, repository and descriptions are set in the workspace.

## Consequences

Users run cargo install tempa-cli and get the tempa binary. tempa-core is a public library on crates.io, so breaking its API needs a semver bump. Publishing needs a CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN secret (release workflow).

## Agent + model

claude-code / claude-opus-5-5

## Context

tempa grew from contract sync (M1) into an agent host (M3: ACP chat, tool policy, worktrees). The owner judged that a drift from the original idea: one contract (AGENTS.md + .tempa/ + tempa.toml) aligned with each coding agent's own format.

## Options

1. Keep building M3. 2. Freeze M3 on a branch and keep its code on main unused. 3. Freeze M3 on branch m3 and remove its code from main. 4. Delete M3 entirely.

## Decision

Option 3. Branch m3 keeps all M3 work (Tasks 1-3 merged there, Task 4 WIP). main returns to the M2 app; the desktop app is frozen as-is. Lifecycle commands stay in the CLI but are optional. Next: add agents (Copilot first), verify target formats against official docs, release and distribution, public readiness.

## Consequences

Resuming M3 means merging m3 again. The CLI is the product; the app gets no new features for now. CI runs once per milestone.

## Agent + model

claude-code / claude-opus-5-5

## Context

tempa check took its base from --base, the CI PR destination, or [ci].base. Task branches started from a milestone branch (m4) were measured against main, so the pre-push hook failed the diff and one-plan gates on work already counted elsewhere.

## Options

1. A TEMPA_BASE env var. 2. A base field in the plan frontmatter. 3. Repo-local git config written by tempa task new (branch.<name>.tempaBase), read by gitx::base_name.

## Decision

Option 3: no new file format, no extra step for the user, and git already scopes it per branch. gitx::base_name gains a root parameter (public API change).

## Consequences

Another clone of the same task branch falls back to [ci].base; pass --base there. CI keeps using the PR destination.

## Agent + model

claude-code / claude-opus-5-5

# Tempa: CI setup (one time)

Local git hooks already run `tempa sync --fix` (pre-commit) and `tempa check` (pre-push). Hooks can be skipped with `--no-verify`, so enforce the contract in CI once you are ready.

## 1. CI step

The step only checks drift and the contract documents. It needs no secrets and runs no tests; keep lint/test in your existing steps. It needs the full git history (`tempa check` diffs against the base branch).

Bitbucket Pipelines:

```yaml
pipelines:
  pull-requests:
    '**':
      - step:
          name: tempa contract
          image: <registry>/tempa:{version}
          clone:
            depth: full
          script:
            - tempa check --contract-only
```

GitHub Actions:

```yaml
on: pull_request
jobs:
  tempa:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container: <registry>/tempa:{version}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
      - run: tempa check --contract-only --base "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"
```

Set `<registry>` once the image hosting is decided. The image version must match `tempa_version` in `tempa.toml`.

## 2. Merge rules

- Require the tempa step to pass (Bitbucket: Minimum successful builds 1; GitHub: required status check).
- Require at least one approval.
- Bitbucket Premium: tick "Prevent a merge with unresolved merge checks".

## 3. Don't

- Don't accept a build status reported from a developer machine in place of this step.
